speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, please sit down. You mentioned an episode of loss of consciousness; can you describe exactly what happened leading up to that moment? Did you lose muscle control before, during, or after the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That onset of syncope immediately after urination is a very specific finding known as micturition syncope. Given your age and the sudden loss of consciousness without confusion, were you standing up quickly when you passed out, or were you sitting or lying down? Also, did you experience any palpitations, chest pain, or shortness of breath right before you collapsed?
